{"source_passages":[{"id":"E118-C","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA, 
and host or bovine immunoglobulins that originate from ascites or cell culture serum. The problem of contaminants of 
animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine 
immunoglobulins pose three different purification problems: albumin because of its abundance; transferrin because of its 
similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.","quote_sha256":"b961c80dda07292a0520ff7fda7116e0af15de4498923da84a9a09cce7336ba4","page_text_start":541,"page_text_end":1292},{"id":"E118-M","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":" Select chromatography techniques that utilize differences in the characteristics of the contaminant and target 
molecule: ion exchange chromatography (IEX) for separation by differences in charge; hydrophobic interaction 
chromatography (HIC) for separation by differences in hydrophobicity; and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) for 
separation by size. See Appendix 9 for an overview of the principles of the chromatography techniques used  
at laboratory scale.","quote_sha256":"65a84cb4b12cfd35901e7245c9be1bef786860db8b80fd1b212b38bd6ee0cb3c","page_text_start":1580,"page_text_end":2047},{"id":"E118-USE","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"For many applications at laboratory scale, contaminant molecules are not always a significant problem. Affinity 
chromatography (AC) will provide sufficient purity and, as long as the presence of any minor contaminants does not 
interfere with the intended application, the purified sample can be used directly.","quote_sha256":"353719de9177ea9d6b00bb5aaac1470a50ea3a083db5f615a4e9284091a1fb2e","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":311}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E119-BH","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Bovine immunoglobulins","quote_sha256":"c5f0af951f4b9ec8b0da709c60833346337b9077da89e58c1ad69fb21a13f71b","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":22},{"id":"E119-B","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Co-purification of host or bovine immunoglobulins is a problem associated with any affinity purification of antibodies 
from a native source or a source to which supplements such as calf serum or bovine serum albumin are added. This 
contamination problem has been largely circumvented in the large-scale manufacture of MAbs for therapeutic use 
through the widespread use of serum-free cell culture systems.","quote_sha256":"3cfa038db9aadb4ae1a986b8a37214e7d658a38d13113b5acf7cd195c1faa4c3","page_text_start":23,"page_text_end":431},{"id":"E119-BI","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Difficulties have also been encountered when murine monoclonal antibodies are the target molecule. The similarities 
between the physical characteristics of the target antibody and the contaminants require careful selection and 
optimization to find the most suitable chromatography technique for purification. Both HIC and IEX can be used.","quote_sha256":"dba348e8e3dd9c320f962ceed1025882e42d5781aeddfdd63f67c570d779a634","page_text_start":432,"page_text_end":772}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E119-AH","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification","quote":"Albumin and transferrin","quote_sha256":"c083fa89230d3d7cd7cc963daeee26692ab7fc3397e3c24aac14c5a7db185051","page_text_start":1382,"page_text_end":1405},{"id":"E119-I","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification","quote":" After an IEX purification, albumin and transferrin can be present if their charge properties are similar to those of 
the target antibody. In some cases, it might be possible to optimize pH and elution conditions in the IEX step to 
improve the separation between the antibody and the contaminants (Appendix 9).","quote_sha256":"8c5889325bb188941f1a6ebace48bfa19be64eea938525ddb6fe835a1d313fd4","page_text_start":1682,"page_text_end":1994},{"id":"E119-A","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification","quote":"Ion exchange and hydrophobic interaction chromatography are two methods used for removing albumin and transferrin, 
separating the molecules on the basis of differences in their isoelectric points or hydrophobicities (see Appendix 9 for the 
principles of these techniques).","quote_sha256":"135c9b62cfaaacc123b3a52e4da443397519cde3b20467d0d70836c6b4e69ce9","page_text_start":1407,"page_text_end":1681},{"id":"E119-H","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification","quote":" Since most monoclonal antibodies are more hydrophobic than albumin and transferrin, HIC can be used to bind the 
antibody and allow these contaminants to wash through the column.","quote_sha256":"650aa882a10835929560563ee04fefca2ec7c25af12fa34e651d6accaebdafd7","page_text_start":1995,"page_text_end":2174}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E120-H","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":"Removal of albumin using Blue Sepharose chromatography media","quote_sha256":"cf0861746d3aa51923ea1e6aaae14a792a33c66c8ac9b81da63b7cd6857f1d8a","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":60},{"id":"E120-W","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":" Do not use Blue Sepharose chromatography media if the immunoglobulin or other target molecule has a

either before or after other purification steps (see Table 4.1). The albumin binds in a nonspecific manner by electrostatic 
and/or hydrophobic interactions with the aromatic anionic ligand, Cibacron Blue F3G-A, coupled to Sepharose.","quote_sha256":"d457eb060e8461acc32b0ed4ed355f2d04d9a626f436e9cd0cb7704ee5cdced4","page_text_start":61,"page_text_end":412},{"id":"E120-U","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":" Use HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL or 5 mL columns to remove host albumin from mammalian expression systems or when 
the sample is known to contain high levels of albumin that might mask the UV absorption of other protein peaks.","quote_sha256":"b9e56ceed5c1f4305abe4124ce7f2066b2a082967db6b07b7fef46d736e6b478","page_text_start":413,"page_text_end":631}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E118-C","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA, 
and host or bovine immunoglobulins that originate from ascites or cell culture serum. The problem of contaminants of 
animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine 
immunoglobulins pose three different purification problems: albumin because of its abundance; transferrin because of its 
similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.","quote_sha256":"b961c80dda07292a0520ff7fda7116e0af15de4498923da84a9a09cce7336ba4","page_text_start":541,"page_text_end":1292},{"id":"E118-USE","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"For many applications at laboratory scale, contaminant molecules are not always a significant problem. Affinity 
chromatography (AC) will provide sufficient purity and, as long as the presence of any minor contaminants does not 
interfere with the intended application, the purified sample can be used directly.","quote_sha256":"353719de9177ea9d6b00bb5aaac1470a50ea3a083db5f615a4e9284091a1fb2e","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":311},{"id":"E118-M","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":" Select chromatography techniques that utilize differences in the characteristics of the contaminant and target 
molecule: ion exchange chromatography (IEX) for separation by differences in charge; hydrophobic interaction 
chromatography (HIC) for separation by differences in hydrophobicity; and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) for 
separation by size. See Appendix 9 for an overview of the principles of the chromatography techniques used  
at laboratory scale.","quote_sha256":"65a84cb4b12cfd35901e7245c9be1bef786860db8b80fd1b212b38bd6ee0cb3c","page_text_start":1580,"page_text_end":2047}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E119-BH","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Bovine immunoglobulins","quote_sha256":"c5f0af951f4b9ec8b0da709c60833346337b9077da89e58c1ad69fb21a13f71b","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":22},{"id":"E119-B","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Co-purification of host or bovine immunoglobulins is a problem associated with any affinity purification of antibodies 
from a native source or a source to which supplements such as calf serum or bovine serum albumin are added. This 
contamination problem has been largely circumvented in the large-scale manufacture of MAbs for therapeutic use 
through the widespread use of serum-free cell culture systems.","quote_sha256":"3cfa038db9aadb4ae1a986b8a37214e7d658a38d13113b5acf7cd195c1faa4c3","page_text_start":23,"page_text_end":431},{"id":"E119-BI","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Difficulties have also been encountered when murine monoclonal antibodies are the target molecule. The similarities 
between the physical characteristics of the target antibody and the contaminants require careful selection and 
optimization to find the most suitable chromatography technique for purification. Both HIC and IEX can be used.","quote_sha256":"dba348e8e3dd9c320f962ceed1025882e42d5781aeddfdd63f67c570d779a634","page_text_start":432,"page_text_end":772}]}

Both HIC and IEX can be used.","quote_sha256":"dba348e8e3dd9c320f962ceed1025882e42d5781aeddfdd63f67c570d779a634","page_text_start":432,"page_text_end":772},{"id":"E119-S","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":" The hydrophobicity of proteins is difficult to predict. Screen several chromatography media with different 
hydrophobicities (e.g., using HiTrap HIC Selection Kit) to find the medium that gives optimal results.","quote_sha256":"6741c581e5bc9fdfd5aad6f728f5e9e5dc438d26155cd1a0bde2846ffd1302a8","page_text_start":773,"page_text_end":984},{"id":"E119-B","pdf_page_1based":119,"pdf_page_index_0based":118,"scope":"Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification","quote":"Co-purification of host or bovine immunoglobulins is a problem associated with any affinity purification of antibodies 
from a native source or a source to which supplements such as calf serum or bovine serum albumin are added. This 
contamination problem has been largely circumvented in the large-scale manufacture of MAbs for therapeutic use 
through the widespread use of serum-free cell culture systems.","quote_sha256":"3cfa038db9aadb4ae1a986b8a37214e7d658a38d13113b5acf7cd195c1faa4c3","page_text_start":23,"page_text_end":431}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E118-M","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":" Select chromatography techniques that utilize differences in the characteristics of the contaminant and target 
molecule: ion exchange chromatography (IEX) for separation by differences in charge; hydrophobic interaction 
chromatography (HIC) for separation by differences in hydrophobicity; and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) for 
separation by size. See Appendix 9 for an overview of the principles of the chromatography techniques used  
at laboratory scale.","quote_sha256":"65a84cb4b12cfd35901e7245c9be1bef786860db8b80fd1b212b38bd6ee0cb3c","page_text_start":1580,"page_text_end":2047},{"id":"E118-USE","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"For many applications at laboratory scale, contaminant molecules are not always a significant problem. Affinity 
chromatography (AC) will provide sufficient purity and, as long as the presence of any minor contaminants does not 
interfere with the intended application, the purified sample can be used directly.","quote_sha256":"353719de9177ea9d6b00bb5aaac1470a50ea3a083db5f615a4e9284091a1fb2e","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":311},{"id":"E118-C","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA, 
and host or bovine immunoglobulins that originate from ascites or cell culture serum. The problem of contaminants of 
animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine 
immunoglobulins pose three different purification problems: albumin because of its abundance; transferrin because of its 
similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.","quote_sha256":"b961c80dda07292a0520ff7fda7116e0af15de4498923da84a9a09cce7336ba4","page_text_start":541,"page_text_end":1292},{"id":"E120-H","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":"Removal of albumin using Blue Sepharose chromatography media","quote_sha256":"cf0861746d3aa51923ea1e6aaae14a792a33c66c8ac9b81da63b7cd6857f1d8a","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":60},{"id":"E120-A","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":"Blue Sepharose 6 Fast Flow or prepacked HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL columns (Fig 4.2) can be used to remove albumin 
either before or after other purification steps (see Table 4.1). The albumin binds in a nonspecific manner by electrostatic 
and/or hydrophobic interactions with the aromatic anionic ligand, Cibacron Blue F3G-A, coupled to Sepharose.","quote_sha256":"d457eb060e8461acc32b0ed4ed355f2d04d9a626f436e9cd0cb7704ee5cdced4","page_text_start":61,"page_text_end":412},{"id":"E120-W","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":" Do not use Blue Sepharose chromatography media if the immunoglobulin or other target molecule has a 
hydrophobicity similar to that of albumin.","quote_sha256":"642c9862aa8781018e99a2c9897854a1a677c97c2e68bd28e1d5aeaadd4e854f","page_text_start":632,"page_text_end":776},{"id":"E120-U","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":" Use HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL or 5 mL columns to remove host albumin from mammalian expression systems or when 
the sample is known to contain high levels of albumin that might mask the UV absorption of other protein peaks.","quote_sha256":"b9e56ceed5c1f4305abe4124ce7f2066b2a082967db6b07b7fef46d736e6b478","page_text_start":413,"page_text_end":631}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E118-C","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA, 
and host or bovine immunoglobulins that originate from ascites or cell culture serum. The problem of contaminants of 
animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine 
immunoglobulins pose three different purification problems: albumin because of its abundance; transferrin because of its 
similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.","quote_sha256":"b961c80dda07292a0520ff7fda7116e0af15de4498923da84a9a09cce7336ba4","page_text_start":541,"page_text_end":1292},{"id":"E118-M","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":" Select chromatography techniques that utilize differences in the characteristics of the contaminant and target 
molecule: ion exchange chromatography (IEX) for separation by differences in charge; hydrophobic interaction 
chromatography (HIC) for separation by differences in hydrophobicity; and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) for 
separation by size. See Appendix 9 for an overview of the principles of the chromatography techniques used  
at laboratory scale.","quote_sha256":"65a84cb4b12cfd35901e7245c9be1bef786860db8b80fd1b212b38bd6ee0cb3c","page_text_start":1580,"page_text_end":2047},{"id":"E118-USE","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"For many applications at laboratory scale, contaminant molecules are not always a significant problem. chromatography (AC) will provide sufficient purity and, as long as the presence of any minor contaminants does not 
interfere with the intended application, the purified sample can be used directly.","quote_sha256":"353719de9177ea9d6b00bb5aaac1470a50ea3a083db5f615a4e9284091a1fb2e","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":311}]}

{"source_passages":[{"id":"E118-C","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA, 
and host or bovine immunoglobulins that originate from ascites or cell culture serum. The problem of contaminants of 
animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine 
immunoglobulins pose three different purification problems: albumin because of its abundance; transferrin because of its 
similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.","quote_sha256":"b961c80dda07292a0520ff7fda7116e0af15de4498923da84a9a09cce7336ba4","page_text_start":541,"page_text_end":1292},{"id":"E118-USE","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"For many applications at laboratory scale, contaminant molecules are not always a significant problem. Affinity 
chromatography (AC) will provide sufficient purity and, as long as the presence of any minor contaminants does not

interfere with the intended application, the purified sample can be used directly.","quote_sha256":"353719de9177ea9d6b00bb5aaac1470a50ea3a083db5f615a4e9284091a1fb2e","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":311},{"id":"E118-C","pdf_page_1based":118,"pdf_page_index_0based":117,"scope":"Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance","quote":"Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA,

animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine

similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.","quote_sha256":"b961c80dda07292a0520ff7fda7116e0af15de4498923da84a9a09cce7336ba4","page_text_start":541,"page_text_end":1292},{"id":"E120-H","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":"Removal of albumin using Blue Sepharose chromatography media","quote_sha256":"cf0861746d3aa51923ea1e6aaae14a792a33c66c8ac9b81da63b7cd6857f1d8a","page_text_start":0,"page_text_end":60},{"id":"E120-A","pdf_page_1based":120,"pdf_page_index_0based":119,"scope":"Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL","quote":"Blue Sepharose 6 Fast Flow or prepacked HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL columns (Fig 4.2) can be used to remove albumin

separation by size. See Appendix 9 for an overview of the principles of the chromatography techniques used
